skill.name: planning-workflow

skill.summary: Plan software projects with detailed markdown workflows before agentic implementation.

content.value_statement: Large AI coding projects fail when implementation starts before the architecture is clear. This skill provides a planning workflow for detailed markdown plans, model review, and task handoff.
actual_capabilities: Explains a planning-first method for complex software projects.
Provides prompts for plan review, revision integration, and multi-model blending.
Lists the core elements of a strong markdown project plan.
Shows example plan documents and AGENTS.md references through GitHub links.
Describes common mistakes when preparing work for coding agents.
Answers workflow questions about tasks, agents, stack choices, and design notes.
limitations: It is a documentation skill, not an automation tool or script package.
It assumes access to specific frontier models and web applications.
Model names and recommended versions may become outdated over time.
It does not validate generated plans or guarantee implementation quality.

use_cases.title: Create a project plan
use_cases.description: Build a detailed markdown plan before starting a complex software implementation.

use_cases.title: Refine a feature design
use_cases.description: Run several review rounds to improve architecture, workflows, and tradeoffs before coding.

use_cases.title: Prepare agent tasks
use_cases.description: Convert a complete plan into self-contained tasks with dependencies for coding agents.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the first plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a detailed markdown plan for this software project. Include goals, user workflows, tech stack, architecture decisions, risks, and implementation phases.

prompt_templates.title: Review the plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this complete markdown plan. Suggest improvements to architecture, reliability, performance, features, and user workflows. Explain the rationale for each change.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate revisions
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate these review notes into the existing markdown plan. Preserve useful details, resolve conflicts, and explain which changes you accepted or rejected.

prompt_templates.title: Blend competing plans
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these competing plans with an open mind. Identify the strongest ideas from each one and produce a stronger unified plan that best serves the project goals.

output_examples.input: A team wants to build a Next.js dashboard but has not chosen workflows or data boundaries.
output_examples.output: The skill guides the user toward a markdown plan with goals, user journeys, stack choices, architecture tradeoffs, and phased implementation tasks.

output_examples.input: A developer has one draft plan and wants a second pass before using coding agents.
output_examples.output: The skill provides review prompts that ask for concrete revisions, rationale, and stronger architecture decisions before implementation starts.

output_examples.input: An operator wants multiple agents to work from a shared plan without losing context.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends converting the plan into self-contained tasks with dependencies, rationale, and enough detail for each agent to proceed.

best_practices: Spend enough time on planning before starting implementation.
Include goals, workflows, architecture decisions, tradeoffs, and rationale in the plan.
Use multiple review rounds until changes become small and incremental.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation from a thin outline.
Skipping review rounds because the first plan looks acceptable.
Creating tasks that depend on context outside the task description.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides planning guidance and prompt templates in markdown.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: It is useful for developers, engineering leads, and operators managing AI coding agents.

faq.question: Does it replace technical judgment?
faq.answer: No. It helps structure planning, but users must still review architecture and implementation decisions.

faq.question: Can it help with small projects?
faq.answer: Yes, but the full workflow is most valuable for complex projects with many dependencies.

faq.question: Does it require specific models?
faq.answer: The source recommends specific frontier models, but the planning method can be adapted to other capable models.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a detailed markdown plan, review notes, revision guidance, and task decomposition advice.
